Legacy blade winding: compiled public domain

Only the legacy spruce and Norway spruce rows reach individualFoliage.
Redwood and sequoia use recursiveFoliage. The legacy path uses style 0.
Lengths below are local metres; world placements come after this winding
calculation. The accompanying producer checks the fixed row assumptions
and every possible blade phase. It does not sample tree seeds.

Envelope bounds

Seed.draw is in [0,1), and swing is in [-1,1). Tree heights are 4..13 m.
A primary branch has length between
  4 * .30 * (1-.88) * (1-.15) = .1224
and
  13 * .30 * (1+.15) = 4.485.
There are three primary segments. A Norway branchlet is at least
  (.1224/3) * 1.1 * (1-.4) * (1-.2) = .0215424
metres long, before its two segments are made. Joint radii use the WHOLE
limb length, not the segment length (grow.go, sleeve.piece). Its smallest
nonterminal leaf joint is .12 of that, above .0025 m. The primary sleeves
and all upper bounds also satisfy the looser shared bounds:
  foot > .002; tip >= 0; both radii < 1; segment length < 2.
The producer checks these inequalities against both compiled rows.

There are at most 12000 blades and 1500 supporting twigs. Midpoint placement
keeps 1-up above 1/3000, apart from rounding much smaller than the margins
used below. Interpolation therefore gives radius > 6e-7 m, blade length
l > 8e-8 m, and width w=.12*l > 9e-9 m. Length is capped at .025 m.
Every generated coordinate has magnitude below 2 m.

Nonzero ideal triple

Let c=cos(turn), s=sin(turn), C=cos(2.4*i), S=sin(2.4*i), using the same
rounded trig results as the construction. Before coordinate rounding,
the three edges are
  U = (-2*w*c, 0, 2*w*s)
  V = (-w*c, w, w*s)
  W = (l*s*C-w*c, l*S, l*c*C+w*s).
Their triple is -2*w*w*l*C*(c*c+s*s). Even blade indices negate way;
that reverses this sign while preserving its absolute magnitude.

Go 1.26.10 on Darwin/ARM64 uses math/sin.go for both trig functions;
math/stubs.go disables archSin and archCos. For turn in [0,2*pi], their
shared argument reduction leaves |z|<.786, z*z<.618. One function takes
the cosine polynomial branch. Bounding its six Horner coefficients gives
an absolute tail below .043, so that branch has magnitude greater than
  1 - .5*.618 - .618*.618*.043 > .67.
Consequently c*c+s*s > .4, without assuming a sampled accuracy figure.
The retained Go producer exhausts i=0..11999 and finds |C|>5e-5. It also
checks the phase sine and cosine stay below the coordinate bound 1.02.
The ideal triple therefore has magnitude greater than 4e-5*w*w*l.

Coordinate and evaluation rounding

Use u=2^-53. Treat the already computed root as a common exact translation.
Products and sums on coordinates below 2 m perturb each computed edge
component by less than 2e-15 m. U.Y remains exactly zero. Expanding the
four remaining determinant terms bounds the coordinate perturbation by
less than 1e-13*w*l, including products of perturbations. Floating point
evaluation of the triple adds less than 60*u*w*w*l.

At w>9e-9, their sum is less than half the ideal magnitude:
  1e-13/(4e-5*9e-9) + 60*u/(4e-5) < .28.
Thus the computed triple cannot be zero. Changing <0 to <=0 chooses the
same winding throughout this compiled public recipe domain.

Limits and reproduction

This is a numerical argument, not a botanical measurement. It does not
cover arbitrary private sprays, new legacy species, altered row ranges,
a different blade budget, or a changed grammar. Review those assumptions
when the recorded sources change.

Copy legacy_blade_phase_domain_sample_test.go into manufacture, run
  go test -count=1 -v -run '^TestDiagnosticLegacyBladePhaseDomain$' ./manufacture
and remove the temporary copy. The appended provenance records the actual
run, toolchain and source hashes. Sampling seeds is not a replacement for
the interval argument and exhaustive phase check.
